1. sshd-hardening  [access-critical]  fixes SSH-001, SSH-003, SSH-005
   Allow key logins only, refuse root and limit auth tries with an early sshd drop-in
   create   /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/00-stackward-hardening.conf (0644)
            checked first with: sshd -t -f <new file>
            --- /dev/null
            +++ b/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/00-stackward-hardening.conf
            @@ -0,0 +1,6 @@
            +# Written by stackward: plan step sshd-hardening, fixes SSH-001, SSH-003, SSH-005.
            +# Named to sort first: sshd keeps the first value it reads. Remove this
            +# file and reload ssh.service to undo.
            +PasswordAuthentication no
            +PermitRootLogin no
            +MaxAuthTries 3
   run      systemctl try-reload-or-restart ssh.service
            # load the new settings; running sessions stay open
   restarts ssh
   note     sshd runs under socket activation (ssh.socket); the drop-in sets no port or listen address, so reloading ssh.service is enough and ssh.socket is left alone.
   note     Existing SSH sessions stay open. Before you confirm, log in again in a new session with your key: that is the proof the change works.
   note     Ubuntu 22.04 and later and Debian 12 and later; older OpenSSH reads KbdInteractiveAuthentication differently.
   undo     Remove the drop-in and reload ssh.service; the earlier values return for new logins.
            rm -f /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/00-stackward-hardening.conf
            systemctl try-reload-or-restart ssh.service

2. lock-default-user  [access-critical]  fixes USR-003
   Lock the cloud image's default account once another admin account is proven
   run      usermod --shell /usr/sbin/nologin ubuntu
            # refuse a login shell
   run      mv -T /home/ubuntu/.ssh/authorized_keys /home/ubuntu/.ssh/authorized_keys.stackward-locked
            # move the authorized keys aside, so no key logs in
   note     Apply it from an SSH session of the admin account that stays (logged in with its key): the lockout guard refuses it from any other session, and from the account it locks.
   note     Running sessions of ubuntu stay open; new logins are refused.
   note     ubuntu keeps its NOPASSWD sudo line: taking sudo away is on the never touched list. Nobody can log in as ubuntu to use it, but USR-003 keeps naming it until you remove the line by hand.
   undo     Move the authorized keys files back, unlock the password if the step locked it, and put the old shell back.
            mv -T /home/ubuntu/.ssh/authorized_keys.stackward-locked /home/ubuntu/.ssh/authorized_keys
            usermod --shell /bin/bash ubuntu
